name: Erioneuron
look_here_first: HAIRY WOOLLYGRASS — SHORT, UPRIGHT WHITE HEADS ABOVE A LOW TUFT. Look for a small warm-season perennial clump, often 10–30 cm tall on shallow limestone or gravel, with tight narrow folded leaves bearing pale/white hardened margins. Thin, mostly leafless flower stalks rise above the basal blades, ending in small dense pale-to-purplish, club-shaped heads of SEVERAL closely packed, woolly spikelets. A mature spikelet typically has 4–12 florets in the UT Williamson County material; each fertile lemma has THREE hairy veins, fine long hairs below, a tiny apical notch and ONE short awn. The two relatively smooth glumes are SHORTER than the lowermost floret. The true leaf collar LIGULE IS A FRINGE OF HAIRS (very short in the UT local treatment), NOT a large membrane. Confirm the glumes/lemma/awn under 10–20×, not from an overview photo.

priority: Find an actual low tuft and the separate slender nearly leafless stalk holding a tight pale woolly flowerhead.
Confirm white cartilaginous folded blade margins and tiny HAIR-FRINGE ligule, not membrane.
Take one mature spikelet to 10–20×; count florets; find TWO relatively hairless glumes shorter than first floret.
Examine three-nerved hairy fertile lemma, shallow notch and single short awn; compare E. avenaceum deeper lemma notch.
recognition.warning: Long hairs on lemmas/paleas must not be incorrectly labeled as hairy glumes; none of the images show actual dissected mature floret or true ligule.

comparison_lesson.title: Hairy woollygrass: exposed club-head vs ground-level fluffgrass
comparison_lesson.memory_rule: SHORT LOW TUFT + WHITE-MARGINED FOLDED LEAVES + SEPARATE LONG MOSTLY BARE STALKS WITH TIGHT WOOLLY HEADS = Erioneuron candidate. Confirm the SHORTER glumes, HAIRY 3-NERVED lemmas with ONE SHORT AWN and HAIR-FRINGED ligule.
quick_split: FLUFFGRASS / Munroa pulchella (syn. Dasyochloa pulchella): hugs the ground as a radiating, sometimes stoloniferous, very low spiky mat; dense woolly spikelet packets nest DOWN among pungent pointed leaves, not atop long mostly leafless erect stalks. TEXAS TRIDENS / Tridens texanus: a more open/flexuous branched panicle with spaced, hanging multiple-flowered spikelets and often bare lower portions of its panicle branches; it is NOT the short dense club of Erioneuron. LARGE-FLOWERED WOOLLYGRASS / Erioneuron avenaceum: can also carry stalked compact woolly heads; in a mature dissection the lemma notch is DEEPER (about 1–2.5 mm) and its upper glume often reaches or passes the lowest floret, compared with E. pilosum's shallow ~0–0.5 mm notch and both glumes shorter than the lowest floret. GENERAL THREEAWNS / Aristida spp.: three long awn limbs arise from one lemma, unlike hairy woollygrass's one short awn. Color, white hairs, dry gravel habitat and tuft height alone cannot decide identity.
comparison_lesson.guardrail: Only E. pilosum canonical here, E. avenaceum comparison only. Original target-zone range review remains deferred and no county-native status upgrade. Public photo policy excludes original owner image with private-study flag.

what_to_teach_crew: First find the SHORT CLUB-SHAPED WOOLLY HEAD on its OWN slender flower stalk ABOVE a low narrow grass tuft.
Compare with Munroa: flowerhead LOW AMONG pungent leaves instead of high on a relatively leafless culm.
Compare with open Texas tridens: spaced dangling spikelets on arching branching panicle instead of a condensed head.
Use a 10–20× lens for mature spikes: glumes are two relatively smooth lower bracts; floral wool comes mainly from lemmas/paleas.
The true LIGULE is a short FRINGE OF HAIRS: do not claim it is a membrane, or mistake long outer collar hairs for the tiny true ligule.
To separate another actual Erioneuron, measure glume versus lowest floret and the shallow/not deep lemma notch with real micro photos.
Keep original photo credits and source restrictions. No invented county PASS, no fabricated arrow anatomical labels.
visual_needs: FULL SAME-PLANT SERIES: entire rooted low clump, one mostly leafless stalk and its attached club-shaped head, with 1-cm ruler and site context.
LEAF BLADE 10×: folded along raised keel, the pair of pale cartilaginous margins, and pointed prowlike tip with a millimeter scale.
TRUE COLLAR 20×: hair-fringe ligule (UT Williamson treatment up to ~0.35 mm) separately from longer COLLAR hairs, with 1-mm scale; no membranous ligule label.
ONE INTACT MATURE SPIKELET 10–20×: approximately 6–11 mm in UT Williamson material, with 4–12 florets counted inside it, two glumes exposed and scale.
GLUMES VS LEMMA 20×: demonstrate the TWO relatively glabrous shorter glumes and a separate THREE-NERVED hairy fertile lemma, with hairs correctly attached to the lemma veins.
LEMMA TIP 20×: show a shallow notch (0.5 mm or less) and one tiny awn (often around 0.5–2.5 mm), with measurement; match E. avenaceum deeper notch under the same scale.
PALEA / HAIR DETAIL 20×: isolate a true two-veined palea and its hairy keel from a fertile floret without misidentifying neighboring spikelet bracts.
visual_status: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS — 3 real inspected Joey exact-taxon JPEGs, 2 existing plus 5 new visible gross-structure arrows, Munroa/Tridens source-licensed comparison panels. Anatomically decisive true collar, glumes and lemma macro still missing.

visual_comparison.title: Hairy woollygrass — three real views of the compact stalked head
visual_comparison.subtitle: 3 actual archived, CC BY-NC Joey Santore photos progress from habitat to clump to floral macro, plus 2 clearly OTHER-species comparison photos. 7 arrows only to visible gross structures.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: SHORT LOW TUFT + WHITE-MARGINED FOLDED LEAVES + SEPARATE LONG MOSTLY BARE STALKS WITH TIGHT WOOLLY HEADS = Erioneuron candidate. Confirm the SHORTER glumes, HAIRY 3-NERVED lemmas with ONE SHORT AWN and HAIR-FRINGED ligule.

items.label: 1 · WHOLE STAND — small tufts with short pale heads
items.image_role: Physically installed exact-taxon Joey photo, inspected full-frame: narrow leaves and many small pale heads on long thin flowering stalks
items.caption: Actual dry gravel habitat with clustered low folded blades and multiple skinny flower stalks. The dense whitish heads stand noticeably ABOVE the leaves; some belong to overlapping tufts. The photograph does NOT expose the true roots, ligule or individual lemma veins.
items.why_it_matters: Crew first look: find club-like heads on slender stalks raised above a low bunch, rather than a silver creeping mat.
items.creator: Joey Santore
items.photo_status: 2026-10-22 actual source full-frame pixels inspected. Two NEW arrows restricted to visible full panicle heads and basal leaf group; separate plants may overlap. No rooted connection or microscopic hair origin asserted.

items.label: 2 · ONE TUFT — leaf bases, nearly bare stalks, clustered woolly heads
items.image_role: Physically installed exact-taxon Joey mid-distance whole clump photo inspected for basal leafy tuft, mostly bare thin flowering stems and compact tops
items.caption: Actual grass in rocky soil shows a dense green basal leaf tuft with several nearly leafless flowering stalks topped by compact hairy terminal clusters. This image is NOT a closeup of a measured ligule, leaf edge cross section or 3-nerved lemma.
items.why_it_matters: Memorize the two-storey silhouette: basal narrow leaf fan BELOW, raised little pale heads ABOVE.
items.creator: Joey Santore
items.photo_status: 2026-10-22 actual source JPEG inspected. Three NEW browser arrows on identifiable gross structures. No claim that microscopic ligule or specific glumes can be distinguished.

items.label: 3 · FLOWERHEAD MACRO — overlapping spikelets and visible pale hair
items.image_role: Physically installed exact-taxon Joey macro photo previously reviewed and now independently visually rechecked at full frame
items.caption: Real pale dense club-shaped seedhead above a finger. Individual spikelet-like packets overlap, and conspicuous silky fringes emerge around their floral bracts. DO NOT label every silky fringe as a hairy glume: botanical treatments describe the glumes as relatively smooth, with most characteristic long hairs on the fertile LEMMAS/PALEAS. A dissected spikelet is still required to locate these organs.
items.why_it_matters: Move from the woolly silhouette to individual spikelets before asking where the three lemma nerves, small apical notch and awn are.
items.creator: Joey Santore
items.photo_status: Prior two browser arrow positions rechecked against actual full JPEG: targets land on dense flowering packets and conspicuous pale fringe zones only. Fringed organs cannot yet be assigned glume versus lemma without a dissection.

items.label: 4 · FLUFFGRASS LOOK-ALIKE — low silvery ground starburst
items.image_role: Actual physically installed DIFFERENT species, Munroa pulchella (fluffgrass); comparison view only
items.caption: FLUFFGRASS, NOT hairy woollygrass. Dense silvery whitish woolly flowering units are nestled very LOW within radiating, narrow sharply pointed leafy arms, making a prickly-looking flattened starburst on gravel. Erioneuron's separate flowering heads sit well ABOVE a basal bunch on slender stalks.
items.why_it_matters: Both are pale and woolly in rocky dry ground; compare the position of the flowerhead RELATIVE TO the leaf cluster, not general fluffiness.
items.creator: Don Rideout
items.photo_status: 2026-10-22 actual original Munroa archived JPEG inspected. Other-species photo only, no source image alterations or species-label ambiguity.

items.label: 5 · TEXAS TRIDENS LOOK-ALIKE — loose hanging flower branches
items.image_role: Actual physically installed DIFFERENT species, Tridens texanus; alternate inflorescence architecture comparison only
items.caption: TEXAS TRIDENS, NOT hairy woollygrass. The flowering head has long exposed branching segments and separate hanging multi-flowered spikelet clusters. Contrast that OPEN, arching construction with Erioneuron's compact tuft of several short pale woolly spikelets at the end of a nearly bare culm.
items.why_it_matters: Many dryland grasses have multi-flowered spikelets. Architecture of an entire flowering stalk plus mature glume/lemma detail reduces confusion.
items.creator: Gaiacoyote
items.photo_status: 2026-10-22 actual installed Tridens source JPEG inspected. Comparison only; original rights, photo metadata and native-range flags untouched.

comparison_matrix.title: Erioneuron vs compact dryland grass look-alikes
rows: Low leaf tuft with long relatively bare stalk and compact woolly pale heads held above leaves
Shorter nearly glabrous glumes than lowest floret; 3-nerved hairy lemma with ≤0.5 mm notch and one short awn
Silvery low flattened starburst, woolly spikelet packets down within sharply pointed leaves
Check similar multi-flowered bracts but flowering units stay ground-level among leaves
Separate hanging spikelets on OPEN flexuous branching panicle, not small tight pale clubs
Measure glumes and 3-veined lemma; branch silhouette alone is not enough
Raised woolly heads can strongly resemble E. pilosum
Deep 1–2.5 mm lemma notch, upper glume often reaching lowermost floret; needs dissected mature macro
Wiry heads may mimic a short dryland grass silhouette
Three terminal awn limbs on ONE mature lemma instead of one short awn
